packageRules.description: In-repo libraries must hold the same version in every module. ci.yml does not check that; a split is only visible as a build failure somewhere else, so keep each bump to a single PR that moves every module's go.mod together rather than one PR per module landing at a different time. Everything else in Go is left to the default of one PR per dependency, which is the cadence the per-service dependabot configs used before the consolidation dropped them.
Actions as one grouped PR, as the per-service dependabot configs did.

Images this repository does not build: the ones the stack pulls, and the base images our own Dockerfiles are built FROM. Pinning them by digest is the point of this config: without it a result is a function of the registry as well as the commit, so an old commit re-run later can go red with nothing to bisect. The tag is kept alongside the digest so the file still says what it is running. `dockerfile` is here so a newly added Dockerfile cannot arrive with a floating base -- though until the Renovate app is installed that is aspirational, and .github/scripts/check-base-images.sh is what actually enforces it.

customManagers.description: Images named from Go rather than from compose: testcontainers constants in hilt, piri and sprue, the busybox helper in pkg/snapshot, and smelt's compose generator, whose output is gitignored and so has no file for the docker-compose manager to read. Two forms are matched: a bare quoted reference, and one wrapped in a ${VAR:-...} compose default, which the generator emits and the first pattern cannot reach. Both REQUIRE an @sha256 digest, which fences this manager by construction: it sees exactly the references this repository has already pinned, and cannot touch the six ghcr.io/fil-forge/<service>:main entries in smelt/pkg/stack/options.go. Those are the published peers an itest run is meant to be tested against, and pinning them would turn that compatibility check into a slower copy of e2e.
